purpose: Dacomitinib is used to treat a type of lung cancer called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread to other parts of the body. It is specifically for patients whose cancer has certain changes (mutations) in a gene called EGFR. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have a faulty protein called EGFR that tells them to grow out of control. Dacomitinib works like a targeted missile — it blocks that faulty protein so the cancer cells can no longer get the signal to grow and multiply. Because it targets a specific protein in cancer cells, it can be more precise than traditional chemotherapy.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea (very common), mouth sores or sores inside your mouth, skin rash or acne-like breakouts, dry or peeling skin, nail problems or infections around the nails, feeling tired, nausea, decreased appetite, and dry eyes or eye irritation.
warnings: Serious lung problems (called interstitial lung disease) can occur — tell your doctor right away if you have new or worsening shortness of breath or cough. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period after stopping. It can also cause liver problems, so your doctor will monitor your blood tests regularly. Avoid taking antacids (like Tums or Maalox) at the same time as this medication, as they can reduce how well it works.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 45 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time — do not double up. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have bothersome side effects.
